To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new incoherent broadband cavity enhanced absorption spectrometer (IBBCEA) has been developed to measure the optical hygroscopic growth of aerosols.

we developed a blue light-emitted diode based incoherent broadband cavity enhanced absorption spectroscopy instrument for the measurement aerosol extinction coefficient and applied it to study the hygroscopic growth of ammonium sulfate particles.

the performance of a novel incoherent broad band cavity enhanced aerosol extinction spectrometry system was evaluated with a laboratory-generated monodisperse polystyrene sphere aerosol and the relative humidity dependence of the aerosols optical hygroscopic properties was measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel IBBCEAS instrument for the measurement and characterization of aerosol optical properties.
the development of an IBBCEAS instrument and its application to the measurement of aerosol hygroscopicity.
the development of an incoherence-based broadband cavity absorption spectrometer (IBBCEA) for the measurement of aerosol extinction coefficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of a blue light emitting diode based incoherent broad band cavity enhanced absorption spectroscopy instrument that has been used to measure the aerosol optical hygrscopicity.
IBBCEAS is a promising method to measure the aerosol extinction coefficients at different wavelengths with high accuracy.
IBBCEAS has been successfully developed for the measurement of aerosol extinction coefficient and optical hygroscopic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed aerosol extinction spectrometers have the potential for long-term field measurements with high accuracy and high sensitivity.
we have successfully developed a blue LED-based incoherent broadband cavity-enhanced extinction spectrometer for aerosol extinction coefficient measurement at 461 nm.
the developed IBBCEAS system can be used as an independent instrument to measure the extinction coefficient at λ =461   nm with a precision better than 5% and an accuracy better than 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developed instrument can measure the aerosol extinction spectrum with a high precision and a high sensitivity.
IBBCEAS is a promising technique for the measurement of aerosol extinction coefficient, especially for those aerosol species with low extinction coefficients.

a blue light-emission-based IBBCEAS instrument can be developed for the measurement of aerosol extinction coefficient and its RH dependence with a detection limit of 5×10-11  cm- 1 and a time resolution of 84 s.
